items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, well I can do what he taught me.

ctx.x: Yes, it's a folk dance, you know, heel-toe, heel-toe kind of thing, you see. Anybody that was familiar with clog dancing, that's what it's all about, anybody's familiar with old Irish folk dancing or anything in that category, they're very familiar with the heel-toe. And you find a lot of heel and toe in tap dancing. Bo Jangles -- Bill Robinson --
Yes, his dancing is based on that.

items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I had got into -- I knew him from the Rhythm Club. As I say, the gaming room in the Hoofer's Club.

ctx.x: Yes. And we were trying to keep one of the songs from the Hoofer's Club fraternity which was introduced by, written especially for, Bill Bojangles Robinson, about tap dancing and how, when he was acquiring his idea of calling the tap dancing tap dancing, and in other words, I'm doing his degree, of the Depression at that time.

items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: If he taught you any tap step... you could go into the lobby of the theater or wherever he was playing in New York City at that time, and see him tap dance. And try to learn yourself some of the tap steps.

ctx.x: Yes. Well, you know, he was the Mayor of Harlem, you see, and he was a great champion of the tap dancing, because he introduced the tap dancing from the Hoofer's Club. He was in the fraternity.

Yes. And we were trying to keep one of the songs from the Hoofer's Club fraternity which was introduced by, written especially for, Bill Bojangles Robinson, about tap dancing and how, when he was acquiring his idea of calling the tap dancing tap dancing, and in other words, I'm doing his degree, of the Depression at that time.
